title: sha2 0.11 upgrade in the osf crate
summary: The osf crate bumps its sha2 dependency from 0.10 to 0.11, which pulls the RustCrypto digest 0.11 generation into the workspace lockfile. That generation replaces generic-array with hybrid-array, adds const-oid, and drops version_check; block-buffer, crypto-common and cpufeatures move with it. No source file changes, so the hashing call sites in osf keep their existing shape and only the crate graph underneath them moves.

lanes.label: osf crate
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf
lanes.summary: The crate whose manifest changed. Its source is untouched; only the sha2 requirement moves from 0.10 to 0.11.

lanes.label: RustCrypto crates
lanes.subtitle: crates.io

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf
nodes.summary: The workspace crate that depends on sha2. Only its Cargo.toml changed; the Rust sources that call the digest API are unchanged in this diff.

nodes.label: sha2
nodes.summary: The SHA-2 implementation crate. The version bump is the whole point of the change; its public surface is what osf compiles against.

nodes.label: digest
nodes.summary: The hashing trait layer sha2 builds on. In 0.11 it gains a const-oid dependency and stops depending on generic-array directly.

nodes.label: block-buffer
nodes.summary: Block buffering used by the digest stack. Its backing array crate switches from generic-array to hybrid-array.

nodes.label: crypto-common
nodes.summary: Shared digest traits and types. It drops generic-array and typenum in favour of hybrid-array.

nodes.label: cpufeatures
nodes.summary: Runtime CPU feature detection used by sha2 to select accelerated backends.

nodes.label: hybrid-array
nodes.subtitle: 0.4.15 (new)
nodes.summary: The array abstraction that replaces generic-array across the 0.11 digest generation. Newly present in the lockfile.

nodes.label: const-oid
nodes.subtitle: 0.10.2 (new)
nodes.summary: Const-friendly object identifier support, newly pulled in by digest 0.11.

nodes.label: generic-array
nodes.subtitle: 0.14.7 (removed)
nodes.summary: The old array abstraction, no longer reachable once block-buffer and crypto-common move to hybrid-array.

nodes.label: version_check
nodes.subtitle: 0.9.5 (removed)
nodes.summary: A build-time Rust version probe that only generic-array needed; it leaves the graph with it.

nodes.label: Cargo.lock
nodes.subtitle: resolved dependency graph
nodes.summary: The lockfile records the resolved versions and checksums for the whole workspace. This change rewrites the sha2 subtree and removes the entries that are no longer reachable.

nodes.label: Cargo resolver
nodes.subtitle: cargo build / cargo update
nodes.summary: Reads the manifest requirement and the lockfile, then selects a compatible version set. It is the actor that turns the manifest edit into the lockfile rewrite.

edges.label: sha2 = "0.11"
edges.summary: The manifest requirement moves from the 0.10 line to the 0.11 line. This single line is what re-resolves the whole digest subtree.
sha2 0.11 is built against digest 0.11, so the trait layer moves with it.
digest 0.11 pulls block-buffer 0.12 for its buffering layer.
digest 0.11 depends on crypto-common 0.2 for shared digest types.
A new dependency edge introduced by digest 0.11.
block-buffer 0.12 buffers into hybrid-array instead of generic-array.
crypto-common 0.2 is generic over hybrid-array rather than generic-array.
sha2 still probes CPU features at runtime, now against cpufeatures 0.3.
The old array dependency is gone from block-buffer's entry.
crypto-common no longer depends on generic-array.
version_check was only reachable through generic-array, so it leaves the graph with it.
The resolver reads the crate manifest to learn the sha2 requirement.
The resolver rewrites the lockfile with the newly selected versions, checksums and dependency lists.
